scenes.heading: Building a content and posting schedule that performs

sents.d: Building a content and posting schedule that performs
Consistency and timing matter more than posting volume alone.

scenes.heading: Plan a week or two ahead

sents.d: A content calendar planned a week or two ahead, rather than posting reactively day to day, makes it much easier to maintain a consistent schedule and spot gaps before they become a quiet week that hurts subscriber retention.

Tracking which posting times and content types actually perform best for a specific creator's audience — rather than assuming general best practices apply universally — lets you refine the schedule with real data over time.
Building in a content buffer for busy weeks or unexpected gaps protects against the account going quiet, which is one of the more common causes of subscriber churn.

take: Plan ahead, follow the data and keep a buffer.
